reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms that Sn addition promotes BCC phase formation in FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx, but it explicitly reports decreased remanence and characterizes the alloys as soft magnets for high-temperature use, with no mention of increased coercivity or domain wall pinning. The key premise that FCC/BCC interfaces increase coercivity is unsupported and contradicts the soft magnetic behavior described.
premises: Sn addition to FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 promotes BCC phase formation, yielding a mixed FCC+BCC structure
The FCC/BCC interfaces act as domain wall pinning sites
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys have coercivity ≤100 Oe
